correction.text: the provinces the Anhui clique page lists, 1916-1920

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Anhui row. The page's provinces: Zhejiang (Lu Yongxiang), Shanghai (He Fenglin as Military Commissioner), Shaanxi (Chen Shufan, nominal governor), Shandong ('subservient to Duan Qirui'), Anhui (Ni Sichong), and 'Gansu, Fujian and Zhang Jingyao's Hunan reliant on the Anhui Clique', plus the Upper Yangtze Garrison in western Hubei. No infobox area; the page gives no dated holdings except Li Houji's Fujian 1914-1923 and Zhang Guangjian's Gansu 1914-1920.

New keyframe: after the 1920 defeat the clique's provinces were 'eventually annexed by the Zhili clique by the summer of 1924'; Fujian went in March 1924 (Zhili page), Zhejiang and Shanghai on 12 October 1924. Gansu's Anhui governor ended in 1920 (the page's table) and the pages show no later Anhui hold on Shaanxi or Hunan, so those three are dropped from 1921 (a reading; a gap-filler should open Duan Qirui).
New keyframe: only Shandong is left by the end of 1924; 'Zheng Shiqi ruled until 1925 when he transferred it to Fengtian's Zhang Zongchang per agreement with Duan'.

ledger.note: 1916: the Anhui clique forms around Duan Qirui. 'Active: 1916-1920' on the infobox; 'after the death of Yuan Shikai and the end of the Constitutional Protection War, Premier Duan Qirui would become Premier of the Republic'. The Anfu Club was 'Formed on 7 March 1918 by Xu Shuzheng and Wang Yitang'. The page gives no territory by year: the region is the provinces it names.

region.text: Outer Mongolia, 'reconquered' by Xu Shuzheng's expedition

ledger.note: 1919 (bridging): the page's table says Xu Shuzheng 'Led expedition that reconquered Mongolia and temporarily brought it back under control'; only the Border Defence Army / National Stabilisation Army divisions are dated '1919-1920', so the year is the researcher's reading, not a page date.
14 July 1920: the Zhili-Anhui War begins ('July 14, 1920 - July 23, 1920'); the page names Zhuozhou, Gaobei, Beicang, Langfang and Nanyuan.
23 July 1920: the Anhui clique is beaten. 'On July 19, 1920, Duan Qirui realized the fight was over and resigned'; 'the defeat and surrender of the Anhui clique'.
1920 (bridging): the Anhui expedition's hold on Mongolia ends with the clique's defeat; the pages opened date neither the withdrawal nor the Soviet and Ungern events of 1921.

By summer 1924 (bridging): all the Anhui provinces 'were eventually annexed by the Zhili clique by the summer of 1924'; the page dates none of them (Zhang Guangjian's Gansu governorship ends in 1920 in its table). Which of these four went when is not on the pages.

March 1924: Fujian. 'Sun Chuanfang gained Fujian in March 1924' (Zhili clique page); Li Houji was governor 1914-1923 and Fujian was 'reliant on the Anhui Clique' (Anhui clique page, whose source this event cites for the clique side).

12 October 1924: Zhejiang and Shanghai fall. The First Jiangsu-Zhejiang War 'ended on 12 October 1924 with an Anhui defeat'; Lu Yongxiang governed Zhejiang through its provincial army and He Fenglin was Military Commissioner of Shanghai.

1925: the last province goes. 'Zheng Shiqi ruled until 1925 when he transferred it to Fengtian's Zhang Zongchang per agreement with Duan'; the Second Zhili-Fengtian page: 'Duan gave Shandong, the last Anhui-held province, to Zhang as a token of their alliance'.

1925: the Anhui clique has no province left. The infobox says 'Disbanded: 1926' and 'They eventually removed him from power and his last followers joined the Fengtian clique'; Duan Qirui led the provisional government that Feng Yuxiang and Zhang Zuolin picked in 1924-1926.

wars.name: Zhili-Anhui War
wars.outcome: Zhili and Fengtian victory: 'Destruction of the Anhui clique'; Duan Qirui resigned on 19 July 1920.
wars.note: 14-23 July 1920; the page says the clique 'lacked national leadership for the next four years' (Anhui clique page).

wars.name: First Jiangsu-Zhejiang War
wars.outcome: Anhui defeat on 12 October 1924: Zhejiang and Shanghai pass to Sun Chuanfang and the Zhili clique.
wars.note: 3 September - 12 October 1924 (the Second Zhili-Fengtian page names it the prelude).

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from three pages (the Second Zhili-Fengtian War page, opened for the Fengtian dossier, supplies the Shandong gift). Cliopatria has no Anhui row. The pages give almost no territory by year: the 1916 region is the list of provinces the Anhui page names (reliant provinces included), the losses are dated only where the Zhili page dates them (Fujian March 1924, Zhejiang and Shanghai 12 October 1924), and Shandong 1925. Not settled: (1) the clique's origin in 1916 and the Constitutional Protection War; (2) the Mongolia expedition's dates (the occupation events are confidence 1 and cite the war page only to close it); a gap-filler should open Xu Shuzheng and 'Mongolia under Chinese rule'; (3) when Shaanxi, Gansu and Hunan were lost; (4) the page's end 'Disbanded: 1926' against the last province going in 1925; (5) the Anhui clique's Fujian (Li Houji to 1923) against Sun Chuanfang's March 1924 gain. Counterpart 'great-mongol-state' is the Cliopatria row (Bogd Khanate, 1912-1925). Gazetteer: the region 'Outer Mongolia' is used (review ea-08-x, 2026-10-25: changed from 'Mongolian Plateau', which also takes in Inner Mongolia).
